headline: March 1996: EU bans British beef exports as the BSE crisis threatens a £3.5 billion industry
why: The ban damaged agriculture, food exports and consumer confidence.

headline: May 1996: Railtrack floats at 380p in a £1.9 billion privatisation
why: The flotation became a defining test of UK rail privatisation and retail share ownership.

headline: August 1996: UK RPI inflation falls at 2.1%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: November 1996: BT agrees a $20 billion merger with MCI to create a transatlantic telecom giant
why: The proposed deal signalled the global consolidation race in telecoms.

headline: February 1997: UK RPI inflation falls at 2.7%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: May 1997: Bank of England gains rate-setting independence after Labour wins a 179-seat majority
why: Independent monetary policy permanently changed how UK rates and bank shares were priced.

headline: July 1997: Thailand abandons its 10-year baht peg, igniting a crisis that cuts the currency 60% by October
why: The currency collapse spread across Asia, damaging growth and UK companies with major regional exposure.

headline: December 1997: Guinness and Grand Metropolitan complete a £24 billion merger to create Diageo
why: The deal created the world’s largest spirits group and a future FTSE heavyweight.

headline: February 1998: UK CPI inflation rises at 1.6%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: June 1998: Bank of England raises Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 7.5%
why: The change altered bank margins, borrowing costs, sterling and equity valuations.

headline: September 1998: Wall Street rescues LTCM with $3.6 billion as its leveraged bets threaten global markets
why: The rescue showed how hedge-fund leverage could endanger major banks and markets.

headline: October 1998: Bank of England starts an emergency easing cycle, cutting rates to 7.25%
why: The cut marked a policy turn as Russia and LTCM weakened global demand.

headline: January 1999: Euro launches at $1.17, creating a single currency for 11 countries
why: The euro reshaped European trade, currency markets and banking strategy.

headline: June 1999: Vodafone completes its $62 billion AirTouch takeover, then the world’s largest corporate deal
why: The deal made Vodafone the leading global mobile operator.

headline: July 1999: UK begins selling 395 tonnes of gold near a 20-year price low
why: The auctions became one of Britain’s most controversial reserve-management decisions.

headline: December 1999: FTSE 100 closes at a record 6,930.2 as the dot-com boom peaks
why: The record captured the extraordinary valuation of telecom and technology shares.

headline: February 2000: Vodafone wins Mannesmann for about €180 billion in the largest takeover ever
why: The acquisition defined Vodafone’s global expansion but left a huge integration burden.

headline: March 2000: Nasdaq peaks at 5,048 before the dot-com bubble bursts
why: The reversal destroyed telecom and technology valuations worldwide.

headline: September 2000: Fuel protests disrupt UK supplies as petrol prices approach 80p a litre
why: Blockades exposed the economy’s vulnerability to fuel distribution and taxation.

headline: December 2000: GlaxoSmithKline is created with a market value of roughly £114 billion
why: The new group immediately became one of Britain’s largest listed companies.

headline: March 2001: Dot-com collapse pushes the Nasdaq more than 60% below its peak
why: Telecom overinvestment and collapsing valuations changed capital allocation for years.

headline: May 2001: Bank of England cuts Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 5.25%
why: The change altered bank margins, borrowing costs, sterling and equity valuations.

headline: September 2001: 9/11 attacks send the FTSE 100 down 5.7% in one session
why: The attacks triggered a global recession scare and abrupt repricing of risk.

headline: December 2001: Enron files for bankruptcy with $63.4 billion of assets
why: The failure transformed audit, governance and credit-risk standards worldwide.

headline: February 2002: UK CPI inflation falls at 1.5%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: June 2002: WorldCom reveals a $3.8 billion accounting fraud
why: The fraud deepened the telecom bust and damaged confidence in corporate accounts.

headline: July 2002: WorldCom files the largest-ever US bankruptcy with $107 billion of assets
why: The bankruptcy intensified losses across telecom lenders and equipment suppliers.

headline: October 2002: FTSE 100 falls below 3,700 as the post-dot-com bear market reaches its nadir
why: The collapse reset equity valuations and pension-fund risk appetite.

headline: March 2003: US-led invasion of Iraq sends oil above $30 a barrel
why: War risk supported energy prices while weighing on global growth expectations.

headline: May 2003: SARS outbreak cuts Asian travel and growth as more than 8,000 cases are recorded
why: The outbreak hit Asian activity and exposed global businesses to epidemic risk.

headline: July 2003: Bank of England cuts Bank Rate to 3.5%, its lowest since 1955
why: Cheaper money supported the housing and consumer recovery.

headline: December 2003: UK CPI inflation holds at 1.3%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: March 2004: Shell chairman quits as a 4.47 billion-barrel reserves overstatement rocks the oil major
why: The scandal destroyed management credibility, triggered governance reform and paved the way for group unification.

headline: May 2004: European Union expands from 15 to 25 members, adding 75 million consumers
why: The enlargement expanded trade, labour mobility and investment opportunities.

headline: July 2004: Brent crude breaks above $40 a barrel as global demand accelerates
why: The oil upswing lifted cash flows and investment across UK energy majors.

headline: November 2004: Vodafone launches 3G services across 13 European countries
why: The launch opened a new mobile-data era after years of costly spectrum investment.

headline: March 2005: BP Texas City refinery explosion kills 15 people and injures more than 170
why: The disaster led to billions in costs and a lasting overhaul of BP’s safety culture.

headline: June 2005: Oil reaches $60 a barrel for the first time
why: The price surge transformed energy-sector profits and investment plans.

headline: July 2005: Royal Dutch and Shell Transport unify into a single £120 billion company
why: Unification simplified governance after the reserves scandal.

headline: October 2005: BP reports quarterly replacement-cost profit of $6.53 billion
why: Record oil prices delivered unprecedented cash generation.

headline: February 2006: UK CPI inflation rises at 2.0%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: June 2006: Asia-led sell-off knocks 146 points off the FTSE 100 in one day
why: The correction ended the market’s early-2006 surge and exposed the sensitivity of miners and financials to global risk.

headline: August 2006: BP shuts Prudhoe Bay, removing up to 400,000 barrels a day of US output
why: Pipeline corrosion damaged BP’s reputation and tightened oil supply.

headline: December 2006: Ferrovial-led consortium completes a £10.3 billion takeover of BAA
why: The deal transferred control of Heathrow and major UK airports to infrastructure investors.

headline: February 2007: HSBC issues its first profit warning as US subprime losses reach $10.6 billion
why: The warning was an early signal that subprime losses could become systemic.

headline: April 2007: Barclays agrees a €67 billion takeover of ABN Amro
why: The bidding war encouraged rivals to take extraordinary balance-sheet risk.

headline: September 2007: Northern Rock suffers Britain’s first bank run in 150 years
why: The run exposed the fragility of wholesale-funded banking models.

headline: October 2007: RBS-led consortium wins ABN Amro with a €71 billion bid
why: The acquisition became one of the defining strategic errors of the financial crisis.

headline: March 2008: JPMorgan rescues Bear Stearns for $10 a share with Federal Reserve backing
why: The rescue showed that a major investment bank could fail within days.

headline: June 2008: RBS raises £12 billion in Europe’s largest-ever rights issue
why: The emergency fundraising revealed how badly the ABN Amro deal had weakened RBS.

headline: September 2008: Lehman collapses with $639 billion of assets as Lloyds agrees a £12.2 billion HBOS rescue
why: The month redefined global finance and forced emergency consolidation in UK banking.

headline: October 2008: UK government commits £37 billion to recapitalise RBS, Lloyds TSB and HBOS
why: The intervention prevented collapse but caused massive shareholder dilution.

headline: January 2009: RBS forecasts a record £24.1 billion loss as the government raises its stake
why: The loss illustrated the scale of destruction caused by the banking crisis.

headline: April 2009: G20 leaders pledge $1.1 trillion to stabilise the world economy
why: The package helped restore confidence in trade and financial markets.

headline: July 2009: Barclays sells BGI to BlackRock for $13.5 billion
why: The deal strengthened Barclays without taking direct UK state capital.

headline: October 2009: UK GDP falls 0.4% in a record sixth consecutive quarter of recession
why: The surprise contraction delayed recovery expectations and reinforced the case for ultra-low interest rates.

headline: February 2010: Kraft completes an £11.5 billion takeover of Cadbury
why: The loss of a British icon intensified debate over foreign takeovers.

headline: April 2010: Deepwater Horizon explosion kills 11 and begins the largest US marine oil spill
why: The spill threatened BP’s survival and transformed offshore regulation.

headline: August 2010: BHP launches a $38.6 billion hostile bid for PotashCorp
why: The bid showed how strongly miners expected long-term agricultural commodity demand.

headline: November 2010: Ireland accepts an €85 billion bailout as the eurozone crisis reaches UK banks
why: The rescue raised fears over European bank exposures and sovereign contagion.

headline: March 2011: Japan’s earthquake and Fukushima disaster erase about 10% from the Nikkei in two days
why: The shock disrupted global supply chains and changed nuclear-energy policy.

headline: May 2011: Glencore floats at a valuation of about £36 billion
why: The blockbuster listing brought a dominant commodities trader into public markets.

headline: August 2011: US loses its AAA rating as the FTSE 100 falls nearly 10% in a week
why: The downgrade and euro crisis triggered a global flight from risk.

headline: October 2011: Bank of England expands quantitative easing by £75 billion to £275 billion
why: The move countered recession risks from the eurozone crisis.

headline: February 2012: UK CPI inflation falls at 3.4%, reshaping the outlook for rates and consumer spending
why: Inflation changed expectations for Bank Rate, real household incomes and domestic company earnings.

headline: April 2012: UK enters a double-dip recession as first-quarter GDP contracts 0.2%
why: The recession weakened domestic demand and reinforced expectations of prolonged monetary support.

headline: July 2012: Draghi pledges to do ‘whatever it takes’ as Spanish 10-year yields approach 7.5%
why: The pledge reversed sovereign panic, lowered borrowing costs and revived European banking and equity valuations.

headline: November 2012: BP agrees a record $4.5 billion US criminal settlement over Deepwater Horizon
why: The settlement crystallised the spill’s legal and financial cost.

headline: February 2013: Moody’s strips the UK of its AAA sovereign rating for the first time since 1978
why: The downgrade reflected weak growth and rising debt after the financial crisis.

headline: May 2013: Glencore completes its $70 billion merger with Xstrata
why: The deal created one of the world’s largest diversified commodity groups.

headline: September 2013: Vodafone sells its Verizon Wireless stake for $130 billion
why: One of history’s largest deals returned tens of billions to shareholders.

headline: December 2013: Federal Reserve begins reducing its $85 billion-a-month bond purchases
why: The taper marked the start of normalisation after the global crisis.

headline: March 2014: Russia annexes Crimea, putting BP’s 19.75% Rosneft stake under sanctions risk
why: The crisis made one of BP’s largest strategic investments vulnerable to sanctions, governance and valuation shocks.

headline: May 2014: AstraZeneca rejects Pfizer’s final £69.4 billion offer
why: The rejection preserved AstraZeneca’s independence and long-term pipeline strategy.

headline: September 2014: Tesco reveals a £263 million profit overstatement
why: The scandal triggered executive departures, investigations and a strategic reset.

headline: November 2014: OPEC refuses to cut production as oil tumbles below $70
why: The decision launched a prolonged oil-price collapse.

headline: February 2015: Swiss Leaks exposes $100 billion held in HSBC’s Geneva private bank
why: The disclosures intensified pressure on tax transparency and bank conduct.

headline: May 2015: Conservatives win a 12-seat majority, ending coalition government
why: The result removed immediate election uncertainty but set up the Brexit referendum.

headline: July 2015: China’s stock market loses about $3 trillion in three weeks
why: The rout threatened commodity demand and Asian earnings.

headline: October 2015: AB InBev agrees a £68 billion takeover of SABMiller
why: The deal created a brewer producing roughly one in three beers worldwide.

headline: January 2016: Brent falls below $28 as China fears wipe 6.1% from the FTSE 100 in the month
why: The sell-off crushed resource earnings and global risk appetite.

headline: June 2016: Brexit vote sends sterling down 8.1% and the FTSE 250 down 7.2% in one day
why: The referendum permanently changed Britain’s trade and investment outlook.

headline: September 2016: SoftBank completes a £24.3 billion takeover of Arm
why: The sale removed Britain’s leading chip designer from the London market.

headline: November 2016: Trump victory sends UK mining sectors up as much as 11.1% and Barclays 4.3%
why: Expectations of US tax cuts, infrastructure spending and higher rates triggered a major rotation into cyclicals.

headline: March 2017: UK triggers Article 50 and starts the two-year Brexit countdown
why: Formal exit negotiations began, affecting investment and sterling.

headline: June 2017: Hung parliament wipes out the government’s majority as sterling falls about 2%
why: The result weakened the government during crucial Brexit negotiations.

headline: August 2017: AstraZeneca shares plunge 15% after the MYSTIC lung-cancer trial disappoints
why: The failure challenged one of the company’s most important growth programmes.

headline: November 2017: Bank of England raises rates to 0.5%—the first increase in a decade
why: The move ended the post-crisis era of continuously falling rates.

headline: February 2018: ‘Volmageddon’ sends the VIX up 116% in one day and triggers a global equity sell-off
why: The episode exposed hidden leverage in volatility-linked investment products.

headline: June 2018: US-China trade war begins with tariffs on $50 billion of Chinese goods
why: The conflict weakened global manufacturing and commodity demand.

headline: September 2018: Comcast wins Sky in a £30.6 billion auction
why: The takeover highlighted the strategic value of UK media assets.

headline: December 2018: FTSE 100 falls 12.5% in its worst year since the financial crisis
why: Brexit uncertainty, trade war and tighter money hit UK equities.

headline: January 2019: Government loses the Brexit vote by 230—the biggest Commons defeat in modern history
why: The defeat intensified uncertainty over Britain’s exit terms.

headline: May 2019: US raises tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods from 10% to 25%
why: The escalation weakened global growth and commodity expectations.

headline: July 2019: Boris Johnson becomes prime minister and pledges Brexit by 31 October
why: Markets repriced the risk of a no-deal exit.

headline: December 2019: Conservatives win an 80-seat majority and sterling jumps above $1.35
why: The result cleared the way for the UK to leave the EU.

headline: January 2020: UK leaves the European Union after 47 years as the first COVID-19 cases reach Britain
why: The departure began a structural change in UK trade and regulation just as a new health shock reached Britain.

headline: May 2020: Oxford-AstraZeneca expands its COVID-19 vaccine trial to more than 10,000 participants
why: The scale-up moved the programme towards decisive efficacy testing and made it central to the global reopening outlook.

headline: August 2020: UK confirms a record 19.4% second-quarter GDP contraction
why: The fall was the deepest among major economies in the first lockdown.

headline: December 2020: UK approves 100 million AstraZeneca doses as a Brexit deal protects £660 billion of trade
why: Vaccine approval improved the reopening outlook while the trade agreement avoided tariffs and quotas on UK-EU commerce.

headline: January 2021: UK begins AstraZeneca vaccinations from a 100 million-dose order during the third lockdown
why: The launch created a credible route to reopening despite severe near-term restrictions on the UK economy.

headline: April 2021: Greensill Capital collapses with more than $5 billion of exposed investor funds
why: The failure highlighted risks in opaque supply-chain finance.

headline: September 2021: UK wholesale gas prices surge more than 70% in a month
why: The shock drove supplier failures, inflation and household cost pressure.

headline: November 2021: Shell combines 2 share classes and moves its tax residence to the UK
why: The simplification improved buyback flexibility and unified the group under one share line and one tax residence.

headline: February 2022: Russia invades Ukraine, sending Brent above $100 a barrel
why: The invasion transformed energy, commodity and inflation expectations.

headline: April 2022: UK inflation reaches 9%, its highest in 40 years
why: The surge forced rapid rate rises and squeezed real incomes.

headline: September 2022: Mini-budget sends sterling to a record low of $1.035 and gilt yields soaring
why: The market revolt forced emergency bond purchases and a change of government.

headline: October 2022: Liz Truss resigns after 44 days, the shortest premiership in UK history
why: The resignation followed the collapse of the mini-budget strategy.

headline: February 2023: Shell reports a record $39.9 billion annual profit
why: The result showed the extraordinary cash generation from the energy shock.

headline: May 2023: Arm chooses Nasdaq for a US IPO expected to raise $8–$10 billion
why: The decision highlighted London’s difficulty retaining high-growth technology listings and reshaped Arm’s ownership future.

headline: September 2023: Arm IPO values the chip designer at $54.5 billion
why: The year’s largest IPO restored Arm to public markets—but in New York, not London.

headline: December 2023: Nearly 200 countries agree at COP28 to transition away from fossil fuels
why: The agreement strengthened long-term transition pressure on the strategy and valuations of energy and mining majors.

headline: February 2024: Arm shares jump 48% in one day after an AI-driven revenue forecast
why: The surge established Arm as a major public-market beneficiary of AI spending.

headline: June 2024: UK inflation returns to the 2% target for the first time in nearly three years
why: The milestone opened the door to rate cuts and improved real-income growth.

headline: July 2024: Labour wins a 174-seat majority, ending 14 years of Conservative government
why: The result brought a major change in fiscal, planning and industrial policy.

headline: October 2024: Budget announces £40 billion of tax rises—the largest increase since 1993
why: The package changed employer costs, gilt issuance and the growth outlook.

headline: January 2025: FTSE 100 closes at a record 8,646.88 after gaining 6.1% in the month
why: The record reflected a rotation into cheaper UK equities and defensive sectors.

headline: June 2025: London’s listed market shrinks as a planned $230 million cobalt IPO is abandoned
why: The cancellation reinforced concern that London was losing listings and capital formation.

headline: July 2025: Wise shareholders approve moving its primary listing to the US, taking an £11.3 billion company from London
why: The vote intensified pressure on London’s ability to retain growth companies.

headline: October 2025: FTSE 100 closes at a record 9,645.62 as financial stocks lead the market higher
why: The new high confirmed renewed investor demand for UK large caps, particularly banks and other value sectors.

headline: March 2026: Iran conflict sends oil up nearly 7% as the FTSE 100 falls 1.2%
why: The disruption revived inflation fears and hit banks while lifting energy majors.

headline: June 2026: FTSE 100 completes a 6th consecutive quarterly gain
why: The streak showed the resilience of UK blue chips through war, inflation and interest-rate volatility.
